title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated images and video to create a synthetic likeness of a real, named attorney, then deployed that likeness at scale across social media platforms to solicit payment for fake legal services. The failure is not one of an AI system making an error inside a legitimate deployment, it is a deliberate misuse of generative AI tools to produce convincing fraudulent personas. The point of harm is the moment a prospective client, already in a vulnerable immigration situation, pays money through an informal transfer app and receives nothing in return.

The scale reported, roughly 6,500 fake profiles removed across three platforms, indicates that the content was produced and distributed faster than platform moderation caught it. Detection came not from the platforms themselves but from a private anti-piracy service hired by the real attorney after clients began calling his office in confusion. A verification mechanism that linked claimed attorney identity to a bar registration or an official contact channel could have interrupted the chain earlier, but no such mechanism is described as having been in place.

What is not established is who is behind the scheme, where it originates, or whether any platform acted improperly, those questions remain open pending the investigation Leal said he intended to initiate with local and federal authorities.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using AI-generated images to impersonate him, offering fraudulent immigration services such as US residency assistance for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity first appeared last October. The situation has dramatically escalated over the past three months.

The scams typically begin with social media videos directing people to contact phone numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters exchange emails and send fake contracts. An anti-piracy company hired by Leal's office has successfully removed approximately 6,500 fake profiles across platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. Leal warns immigrants to be cautious of requests for payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App and advises verifying anyone offering legal services online. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scheme's origin.
